Base, an adjacent angle and the SUM of the two remaining sides are given, so this is Construction I.
Mark D on the ray through Q with \(QD = PQ + PR = 8.5\) cm. Then \(QP + PD = QP + PR\), so \(PD = PR\) and P lies on the perpendicular bisector of seg DR.
Steps of construction :
(1) Draw seg QR of length 4.2 cm.
(2) Draw ray QT such that \(m\angle TQR = 40^\circ\).
(3) Mark point D on ray QT such that \(d(Q, D) = 8.5\) cm.
(4) Draw seg DR.
(5) Construct the perpendicular bisector of seg DR.
(6) Name the point of intersection of ray QT and that perpendicular bisector as P.
(7) Draw seg PR.
\(\triangle PQR\) is the required triangle. On measuring, \(PQ \approx 5.2\) cm and \(PR \approx 3.3\) cm, whose sum is the given 8.5 cm.

Base, an adjacent angle and the SUM of the two remaining sides are given, so this is Construction I.
Mark D on the ray through Y with \(YD = XY + XZ = 9\) cm. Then \(YX + XD = YX + XZ\), so \(XD = XZ\) and X lies on the perpendicular bisector of seg DZ.
Steps of construction :
(1) Draw seg YZ of length 6 cm.
(2) Draw ray YT such that \(m\angle TYZ = 50^\circ\).
(3) Mark point D on ray YT such that \(d(Y, D) = 9\) cm.
(4) Draw seg DZ.
(5) Construct the perpendicular bisector of seg DZ.
(6) Name the point of intersection of ray YT and that perpendicular bisector as X.
(7) Draw seg XZ.
\(\triangle XYZ\) is the required triangle. On measuring, \(XY \approx 4.4\) cm and \(XZ \approx 4.6\) cm, whose sum is the given 9 cm.

Base, an adjacent angle and the SUM of the two remaining sides are given, so this is Construction I. Here the given angle is at C, so the construction is carried out at C.
Mark D on the ray through C with \(CD = CA + AB = 9.8\) cm. Then \(CA + AD = CA + AB\), so \(AD = AB\) and A lies on the perpendicular bisector of seg DB.
Steps of construction :
(1) Draw seg BC of length 6.2 cm.
(2) Draw ray CT on the same side of line BC as A, such that \(m\angle TCB = 50^\circ\).
(3) Mark point D on ray CT such that \(d(C, D) = 9.8\) cm.
(4) Draw seg DB.
(5) Construct the perpendicular bisector of seg DB.
(6) Name the point of intersection of ray CT and that perpendicular bisector as A.
(7) Draw seg AB.
\(\triangle ABC\) is the required triangle. On measuring, \(AC \approx 5.0\) cm and \(AB \approx 4.8\) cm, whose sum is the given 9.8 cm.

The perimeter is given instead of the sum of the two remaining sides, so subtract the base first :
\(AB + AC = 10 - BC = 10 - 3.2 = 6.8\) cm.
That turns the question into Construction I, with the given angle at C. Mark D on the ray through C with \(CD = CA + AB = 6.8\) cm; then \(AD = AB\), so A lies on the perpendicular bisector of seg DB.
Steps of construction :
(1) Draw seg BC of length 3.2 cm.
(2) Draw ray CT such that \(m\angle TCB = 45^\circ\).
(3) Mark point D on ray CT such that \(d(C, D) = 6.8\) cm.
(4) Draw seg DB.
(5) Construct the perpendicular bisector of seg DB.
(6) Name the point of intersection of ray CT and that perpendicular bisector as A.
(7) Draw seg AB.
\(\triangle ABC\) is the required triangle. On measuring, \(AC \approx 4.0\) cm and \(AB \approx 2.8\) cm, so \(AB + BC + CA \approx 10\) cm as required.

Base, an adjacent angle and the DIFFERENCE of the two remaining sides are given, so this is Construction II. Since \(XY - XZ = 2.7\) cm, \(XY > XZ\), so D is taken on the SAME ray as X.
Take D on ray YX with \(YD = XY - XZ = 2.7\) cm. Then Y-D-X and \(YD = XY - XD\), so \(XD = XZ\) and X lies on the perpendicular bisector of seg DZ.
Steps of construction :
(1) Draw seg YZ of length 7.4 cm.
(2) Draw ray YL such that \(\angle LYZ = 45^\circ\).
(3) Take point D on ray YL such that \(YD = 2.7\) cm.
(4) Construct the perpendicular bisector of seg DZ.
(5) Name the point of intersection of ray YL and that perpendicular bisector as X.
(6) Draw seg XZ.
\(\triangle XYZ\) is the required triangle. On measuring, \(XY \approx 9.4\) cm and \(XZ \approx 6.7\) cm, whose difference is the given 2.7 cm.

Base, an adjacent angle and the DIFFERENCE of the two remaining sides are given, so this is Construction II. Since \(PQ - PR = 2.5\) cm, \(PQ > PR\), so D is taken on the SAME ray as P.
Take D on ray QP with \(QD = PQ - PR = 2.5\) cm. Then Q-D-P and \(QD = PQ - PD\), so \(PD = PR\) and P lies on the perpendicular bisector of seg DR.
Steps of construction :
(1) Draw seg QR of length 6.5 cm.
(2) Draw ray QL such that \(\angle LQR = 40^\circ\).
(3) Take point D on ray QL such that \(QD = 2.5\) cm.
(4) Construct the perpendicular bisector of seg DR.
(5) Name the point of intersection of ray QL and that perpendicular bisector as P.
(6) Draw seg PR.
\(\triangle PQR\) is the required triangle. On measuring, \(PQ \approx 7.3\) cm and \(PR \approx 4.8\) cm, whose difference is the given 2.5 cm.

Base, an adjacent angle and the DIFFERENCE of the two remaining sides are given, so this is Construction II. Here \(AC - AB = 2.5\) cm, so the LARGER side is AC, the one not meeting the given angle. D therefore goes on the ray OPPOSITE to ray BA.
Take D on the opposite ray of ray BA with \(BD = 2.5\) cm. Then \(AD = AB + BD = AB + 2.5 = AC\), so \(AD = AC\) and A lies on the perpendicular bisector of seg DC.
Steps of construction :
(1) Draw seg BC of length 6 cm.
(2) Draw ray BT such that \(\angle TBC = 100^\circ\).
(3) Take point D on ray BS, the ray opposite to ray BT, such that \(BD = 2.5\) cm.
(4) Construct the perpendicular bisector of seg DC.
(5) Name the point of intersection of ray BT and that perpendicular bisector as A.
(6) Draw seg AC.
\(\triangle ABC\) is the required triangle. On measuring, \(AB \approx 10.2\) cm and \(AC \approx 12.7\) cm, whose difference is the given 2.5 cm.

The perimeter and the two angles that include the base QR are given, so this is Construction III.
Take M and N on line QR with \(MQ = PQ\) and \(RN = PR\), so that \(MN = PQ + QR + PR = 9.5\) cm. In \(\triangle MQP\), \(MQ = QP\), so \(\angle QMP = \angle QPM\), and their sum is the exterior angle \(\angle PQR = 70^\circ\); hence \(\angle QMP = 35^\circ\). Similarly \(\angle RNP = 40^\circ\).
Steps of construction :
(1) Draw seg MN of length 9.5 cm.
(2) Draw a ray at M making an angle of \(35^\circ\) with MN.
(3) Draw a ray at N making an angle of \(40^\circ\) with NM, on the same side.
(4) Name the point of intersection of the two rays as P.
(5) Construct the perpendicular bisectors of seg PM and seg PN; name the points where they cut line MN as Q and R respectively.
(6) Draw seg PQ and seg PR.
\(\triangle PQR\) is the required triangle. On measuring, \(PQ \approx 3.9\) cm, \(QR \approx 2.0\) cm and \(PR \approx 3.7\) cm, a perimeter of 9.5 cm with \(\angle Q = 70^\circ\) and \(\angle R = 80^\circ\).

The perimeter and the two angles that include the base XY are given, so this is Construction III.
Take M and N on line XY with \(MX = ZX\) and \(YN = ZY\), so that \(MN = 10.5\) cm, the perimeter. As \(MX = XZ\), \(\angle XMZ = \angle XZM\) and their sum is the exterior angle \(\angle ZXY = 46^\circ\); hence \(\angle XMZ = 23^\circ\). Similarly \(\angle YNZ = 29^\circ\).
Steps of construction :
(1) Draw seg MN of length 10.5 cm.
(2) Draw a ray at M making an angle of \(23^\circ\) with MN.
(3) Draw a ray at N making an angle of \(29^\circ\) with NM, on the same side.
(4) Name the point of intersection of the two rays as Z.
(5) Construct the perpendicular bisectors of seg ZM and seg ZN; name the points where they cut line MN as X and Y respectively.
(6) Draw seg ZX and seg ZY.
\(\triangle XYZ\) is the required triangle. On measuring, \(XY \approx 4.0\) cm, \(YZ \approx 3.0\) cm and \(XZ \approx 3.5\) cm, a perimeter of 10.5 cm with \(\angle X = 46^\circ\) and \(\angle Y = 58^\circ\).

The perimeter and the two angles that include the base MN are given, so this is Construction III.
Take P and Q on line MN with \(PM = LM\) and \(NQ = LN\), so that \(PQ = LM + MN + NL = 11\) cm. As \(PM = ML\), \(\angle MPL = \angle MLP\) and their sum is the exterior angle \(\angle LMN = 60^\circ\); hence \(\angle MPL = 30^\circ\). Similarly \(\angle NQL = 40^\circ\).
Steps of construction :
(1) Draw seg PQ of length 11 cm.
(2) Draw a ray at P making an angle of \(30^\circ\) with PQ.
(3) Draw a ray at Q making an angle of \(40^\circ\) with QP, on the same side.
(4) Name the point of intersection of the two rays as L.
(5) Construct the perpendicular bisectors of seg LP and seg LQ; name the points where they cut line PQ as M and N respectively.
(6) Draw seg LM and seg LN.
\(\triangle LMN\) is the required triangle. On measuring, \(LM \approx 4.3\) cm, \(MN \approx 2.8\) cm and \(NL \approx 3.8\) cm, a perimeter of 11 cm with \(\angle M = 60^\circ\) and \(\angle N = 80^\circ\).

Base YZ, the adjacent angle at Y and the SUM of the two remaining sides are given, so this is Construction I.
Mark D on the ray through Y with \(YD = XY + XZ = 10.3\) cm. Then \(YX + XD = YX + XZ\), so \(XD = XZ\) and X lies on the perpendicular bisector of seg DZ.
Steps of construction :
(1) Draw seg YZ of length 4.9 cm.
(2) Draw ray YT such that \(m\angle TYZ = 45^\circ\).
(3) Mark point D on ray YT such that \(d(Y, D) = 10.3\) cm.
(4) Draw seg DZ.
(5) Construct the perpendicular bisector of seg DZ.
(6) Name the point of intersection of ray YT and that perpendicular bisector as X.
(7) Draw seg XZ.
\(\triangle XYZ\) is the required triangle. On measuring, \(XY \approx 6.0\) cm and \(XZ \approx 4.3\) cm, whose sum is the given 10.3 cm.

The perimeter and the two angles that include the base BC are given, so this is Construction III.
Take P and Q on line BC with \(PB = AB\) and \(CQ = AC\), so that \(PQ = AB + BC + AC = 11.2\) cm. As \(PB = BA\), \(\angle APB = \angle PAB\) and their sum is the exterior angle \(\angle ABC = 70^\circ\); hence \(\angle APB = 35^\circ\). Similarly \(\angle CQA = 30^\circ\).
Steps of construction :
(1) Draw seg PQ of length 11.2 cm.
(2) Draw a ray at P making an angle of \(35^\circ\) with PQ.
(3) Draw a ray at Q making an angle of \(30^\circ\) with QP, on the same side.
(4) Name the point of intersection of the two rays as A.
(5) Construct the perpendicular bisectors of seg AP and seg AQ; name the points where they cut line PQ as B and C respectively.
(6) Draw seg AB and seg AC.
\(\triangle ABC\) is the required triangle. On measuring, \(AB \approx 3.8\) cm, \(BC \approx 3.3\) cm and \(AC \approx 4.1\) cm, a perimeter of 11.2 cm with \(\angle B = 70^\circ\) and \(\angle C = 60^\circ\).

No angle is given, so first turn the ratio into lengths. Let the sides be \(2k\), \(3k\) and \(4k\).
\(2k + 3k + 4k = 14.4\), so \(9k = 14.4\) and \(k = 1.6\).
The sides are \(3.2\) cm, \(4.8\) cm and \(6.4\) cm. They satisfy the triangle inequality, since \(3.2 + 4.8 = 8 > 6.4\), so the triangle exists and the three-sides construction can be used.
Steps of construction :
(1) Draw seg BC of length 6.4 cm.
(2) With B as centre and radius 3.2 cm, draw an arc.
(3) With C as centre and radius 4.8 cm, draw another arc cutting the first one; name that point of intersection A.
(4) Draw seg AB and seg AC.
\(\triangle ABC\) is the required triangle, with \(AB = 3.2\) cm, \(CA = 4.8\) cm and \(BC = 6.4\) cm, which are in the ratio \(2 : 3 : 4\) and add up to the given perimeter 14.4 cm.

Base QR, the adjacent angle at Q and the DIFFERENCE of the two remaining sides are given, so this is Construction II. Since \(PQ - PR = 2.4\) cm, \(PQ > PR\), so D is taken on the SAME ray as P.
Take D on ray QP with \(QD = PQ - PR = 2.4\) cm. Then Q-D-P and \(QD = PQ - PD\), so \(PD = PR\) and P lies on the perpendicular bisector of seg DR.
Steps of construction :
(1) Draw seg QR of length 6.4 cm.
(2) Draw ray QL such that \(\angle LQR = 55^\circ\).
(3) Take point D on ray QL such that \(QD = 2.4\) cm.
(4) Construct the perpendicular bisector of seg DR.
(5) Name the point of intersection of ray QL and that perpendicular bisector as P.
(6) Draw seg PR.
\(\triangle PQR\) is the required triangle. It comes out long and narrow: on measuring, \(PQ \approx 13.8\) cm and \(PR \approx 11.4\) cm, whose difference is the given 2.4 cm.
